title: Reading notes
text:
The Reading Notes landing page is for you to curate and maintain any articles, manuals, or media that is related in any way to your research. Ideally, this should be treated like an annotated bibliography. To make the most of this, make sure to include useful keywords and link to any relevant projects (when possible).
Information on making new notes and editing them is below.



To make a new reading note, simply make a copy the existing template and update the contents.
The file also automatically gets added to a table of all such files, which is accessible from the Reading Notes landing page of the website.
This file is also added to the Reading Notes section of each Project landing page.
Creating and editing reading notes will be demonstrated in the video below – when Xyrus has the time!






Video instructions to create and edit reading notes

title: Meeting notes
text:
The Meeting Notes landing page is the place to find any notes from meetings with others in the lab. This makes it easy to track what the overarching goals were and to ensure that any “action items” do not end up lost or forgotten!
Make sure to update this right after (or during) meetings! Additionally, this aids in improving accountability and is an easy spot to reference back to anything that was brought up that needs attention.



Information on making new notes and editing them is below.
Meeting note files are mostly found in their corresponding Project folder. It is recommended to use prior .qmd files as the template, making sure to update the dates and entries inside the copied files!
Meetings associated with specific project tags are listed under the corresponding Projects landing pages, or can be viewed directly from the Meeting Notes landing page.
For meetings not connected with a project, simply copy, paste, and edit the existing template in the Meeting Notes folder.
Creating and editing meeting notes will be demonstrated in the video below.






Video instructions to create/edit weekly notes

title: Lab Notebook
text:
The Lab Notebook landing page is for you to curate and maintain any work you do in the lab, whether it be benchwork or computational. It is crucial that this remains up-to-date and is fantastic practice for generating and maintaining good documentation, which truthfully helps everyone in the lab (including yourself).
Information on making new notes and editing them is below.



While the template for lab notebook entries are in a weekly format, feel free to change this as needed! Also, make sure to tag your entries with the appropriate project, which may mean that you have multiple weekly notes for different projects!
This makes it easier to navigate and hunt useful information as needed! Creating and editing lab notes is (hopefully) fairly easy.
Specifically, if a weekly lab notes file for the present week does not exist1, simply copy, paste (rename the file) and edit the template.
Once created and renamed, the file automatically gets added to a table of all such files, which is accessible from the Lab Notebook and Projects landing pages of the website.
Creating and editing lab notes will be demonstrated in the video below.






Video instructions to create/edit weekly notes
